title: Twitter Timeline
summary: Home timelines at scale: fan out tweets on write into cached per-user timelines, pull celebrity tweets at read time, and merge and rank on request.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Post a tweet (text, media), follow users
Home timeline: recent tweets from followed accounts, newest or ranked
Home timeline p99 < 200 ms; tweet visible to followers within ~5 s

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Reads are 50 times writes, so precomputing timelines pays off, but a single 100-million-follower account would turn one tweet into 100 million writes. That's the core tension.

head: Data
Key
Store
rows: Distributed KV/wide-column (Manhattan at Twitter), sharded by tweet_id

blocks.text: Timelines store only tweet IDs (8 bytes each); tweet bodies are hydrated from a tweet cache at read time. 250M users × 800 IDs × 8 B ≈ 1.6 TB, spread across a Redis fleet with replicas.

blocks.caption: Write path fans out IDs; read path merges cached timeline with celebrity pulls

items: **Write:** store tweet → publish event → fan-out workers fetch followers in pages and `LPUSH` the tweet ID onto each follower's timeline list, trimming to 800.
**Read:** read the user's cached list, merge in recent tweets from followed celebrities (pulled from their user_tweets), hydrate bodies, rank, return a page.

sections.title: Deep dive: push vs pull vs hybrid

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: Hybrid: push for accounts below a threshold (say 100k followers), pull for celebrities at read time and merge. Skip pushing to users inactive for 30+ days and rebuild their timeline on next login.

def home(user):
    ids = redis.lrange(f'tl:{user}', 0, 199)              # pushed
    for celeb in graph.followed_celebrities(user):       # pulled
        ids += user_tweets.recent(celeb, since=ids_oldest(ids))
    return rank(hydrate(dedupe(ids)))[:20]

items: Candidate generation: in-network (the merged timeline) + out-of-network (recommendations from embeddings / graph).
Light ranker filters to ~1,500 candidates; heavy ranker (neural network) scores engagement probability.
Heuristics after ranking: author diversity, remove seen, mix media, filter blocked/muted.
Cache the ranked page per user for a short time so pagination is stable; cursor = position in that ranked list.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: In an interview say ranking exists and where it plugs in; don't spend 10 minutes on ML unless asked.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Replicas; rebuild on miss from followees' user_tweets (slow path)
Partition Kafka by author; autoscale workers on lag; prioritize active users
Local in-process cache for top tweets
Filter at hydration (tombstone check), lazy removal

items.text: 200 ms reads, 5 s freshness, celebrity skew.

items.title: Wrap-up
items.text: Celebrity threshold, inactive users, lag metrics.

items.q: Where does the celebrity threshold come from?
items.a: Tune by cost: when expected fan-out writes exceed the extra read-merge cost across their followers. Often ~100k–1M followers.

items.q: How do you paginate a ranked feed?
items.a: Rank once, cache the ordered ID list for the session, and page through it with a cursor; new tweets show as a 'new posts' banner.
Filter at read time against the follow set; lazily drop entries.
Separate pipeline: tweets → Kafka → inverted index (Earlybird at Twitter), sharded by time.

items: Hybrid fan-out: push for normal users, pull for celebrities.
Timelines hold IDs only; hydrate at read.
Snowflake IDs give time order for free.
Ranking: candidates → light ranker → heavy ranker → heuristics.
Watch fan-out lag and timeline cache hit rate.
